summary: Executable plan for CD-5 in a greenfield repo. I checked the workspace: it has only `.am/` (platform-managed), `.playwright-mcp/` and commit 4ab1bdc. The work follows the approved technical plan's six work packages and turns each into one epic with exclusive write scopes. EPIC-001 lays down the root foundation and the complete C7 Makefile contract. EPIC-002 (scanner), EPIC-003 (API) and EPIC-004 (web) then run in parallel and fill max_concurrency=3. EPIC-005 adds the checked-in fixture and golden harness once the scanner's C1/C3 contracts exist. EPIC-006 wires CI and the root README to the same Makefile targets and runs the acceptance checks. Every epic's acceptance criteria point back to the plan's verification matrix (V-S*, V-F*, V-A*, V-W*, V-I*), so the developer stage can turn them directly into tests and checks.

epics.title: Root foundation and Makefile contract
epics.description:
Owns WP-0. Exclusive write scope: `/.gitignore`, `/.gitattributes`, `/.python-version`, `/Makefile`. Must never touch `.am/**`.

- `.gitignore` lists exactly the entries in plan §4 (FR-007). It includes `.playwright-mcp/` and must NOT ignore `.am/`.
- `.gitattributes` contains `* text=auto eol=lf` and `fixtures/** text eol=lf` (FR-008).
- `.python-version` pins CPython 3.14 at its full patch, e.g. `3.14.Z` (FR-006).
- `Makefile` implements every target in contract C7, with names and commands exactly as written: install*, test*, lint*, format*, build-web, run-*, regen-fixtures, bench-api. Each recipe runs inside its area directory (`$(MAKE) -C` or `cd <area> &&`). Use `uv run --locked` for the Python areas and pnpm for web. Mark targets `.PHONY`. The file must work with both GNU and BSD make, so use no GNU-only functions. `UV_PYTHON` passes through from the environment.

Area targets will fail until their areas exist. That is expected, and integration is gated at CP-2. After this epic, only EPIC-006 may change the Makefile. Deliverable: integration checkpoint CP-1.
acceptance_criteria: `git check-attr eol -- fixtures/x/a.py` reports `lf`, and `git check-attr text -- README.md` reports `auto`.
`make -n test`, `make -n lint`, `make -n install` and `make -n build-web` print the exact C7 commands for each area, in the order scanner, fixtures, api, web.
`git check-ignore .playwright-mcp/x` matches, `git check-ignore .am/README.md` does not match, and `git status` shows no change under `.am/` from this epic.
`.python-version` has one line with a full `3.14.<patch>` version.
The Makefile parses under both GNU make and macOS `/usr/bin/make` (`make -n help` or `make -n test` exits 0).

epics.title: Scanner CLI with deterministic empty report
epics.description:
Owns WP-S. Exclusive write scope: `scanner/**` EXCEPT `scanner/tests/golden/**`, which belongs to EPIC-005.

Create the `dogwatch` uv project:
- `pyproject.toml`:
  - name `dogwatch`, version 0.1.0, `requires-python >=3.11`, `uv_build` backend
  - `[project.scripts] dogwatch = "dogwatch.cli:main"`
  - `[tool.uv] required-version` set to 0.12.x
  - ruff `target-version = "py311"`, mypy `strict` with `python_version = "3.11"`
  - dev dependencies: pytest, ruff, mypy, jsonschema
  - pytest `--strict-markers`, with the `golden` marker PRE-REGISTERED in `[tool.pytest.ini_options] markers`; this is a seam for EPIC-005
  - committed `uv.lock`
- Zero runtime dependencies (FR-009, FR-063).

Modules under `src/dogwatch/`: `__init__`, `__main__`, `cli`, `diagnostics`, `config`, `report`, `output`, plus `py.typed`. They implement:
- C1: CLI, exit codes 0 and 2, exit 1 reserved, `--version`, `python -m dogwatch`.
- C2 and the §6 V0–V4 validation pipeline:
  - R-3: single-identifier name; duplicate, split and nested checks.
  - R-4: not-found means the path does not exist; any other read problem is config-invalid.
  - R-5: TOML line number via the `lineno` attribute, with a regex fallback.
- C3 schema file at `schemas/report-0.1.schema.json`.
- Canonical serialization: `json.dumps(sort_keys=True, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"`, UTF-8 bytes.
- `policy.path` is the basename of the argument; `policy.digest.sha256` is the hash of the raw bytes.
- Atomic output: temp file in the target's directory, fsync, `os.replace`; the temp file is removed on failure.
- `--output -` writes through `sys.stdout.buffer`.
- Output that equals the config is rejected with `dogwatch: error:` (R-2).
- Structure checks use filesystem metadata only. The scanner never opens or imports files under package directories (FR-013a, FR-014).

Also create an empty `scanner/tests/__init__.py`, so `tests.golden` resolves the same way for pytest and for `python -m tests.golden.regenerate`; this is a seam for EPIC-005. Add `tests/conftest.py` with the `repo_root` and `make_config` fixtures. Tests follow V-S1…V-S7. Deliverable: CP-2 for the scanner.
acceptance_criteria: `make lint-scanner` passes (ruff format --check, ruff check, mypy --strict) in a clean clone with only uv installed.

`make test-scanner` passes and deselects `golden`-marked tests. It covers V-S1 (CLI/version/defaults/exit codes), V-S2 (missing, unreadable, invalid UTF-8, malformed TOML with line number, unsupported keys such as `python.rules`/`openapi`, empty, no packages, dotted name), V-S3 (missing dir, file-not-dir, duplicate, split, nested → exit 2 and no output file; zero .py files → exit 0; no `__init__.py` is fine), V-S4 (canonical bytes and report validated against `schemas/report-0.1.schema.json` with jsonschema), V-S5 (unwritable dir, output == config, `--output -`; target untouched, no temp left), V-S6 (child ru_maxrss ≤ 200 MB, unit handled per OS), and V-S7 (open/io.open_code/import_module under package dirs is never called).
`UV_PYTHON=3.11 make test-scanner` and `UV_PYTHON=3.14 make test-scanner` both pass locally.
`uv run dogwatch --version` prints exactly `dogwatch 0.1.0` followed by a newline and exits 0.

Running `dogwatch check --config <minimal valid toml> --output -` twice produces byte-identical stdout with keys in the order findings, policy, scanner, schema_version, LF endings, one trailing newline, no BOM, and `findings: []`.
Missing config prints exactly `dogwatch:config-not-found: <path> does not exist` to stderr, exits 2, and leaves stdout empty.
`scanner/pyproject.toml` registers the `golden` marker and enables `--strict-markers`. `scanner/tests/__init__.py` exists. Nothing is created under `scanner/tests/golden/`.
`uv.lock` is committed, and `[project] dependencies` is empty.

epics.title: Stateless FastAPI health service
epics.description:
Owns WP-A. Exclusive write scope: `api/**`.

Create the `dogwatch-api` uv project:
- `requires-python ==3.14.*`
- runtime dependencies: fastapi, plain uvicorn
- dev dependencies: pytest, httpx, ruff, mypy
- `[tool.uv] required-version`, ruff and mypy strict configured in `pyproject.toml` so the tools run with no arguments
- `[project.scripts] dogwatch-api`
- committed `uv.lock`
- `.env.example` listing DOGWATCH_API_HOST and DOGWATCH_API_PORT

Modules:
- `settings.py`: reads `os.environ`. Defaults are 127.0.0.1 and 8000; the port must be 1–65535. An invalid value exits 1 and names the variable.
- `app.py`: a `create_app()` factory. Sets `openapi_url=/api/v1/openapi.json`, `docs_url=None`, `redoc_url=None`. Produces OpenAPI 3.1.
- `health.py`: GET `/api/v1/health` returns the `HealthStatus` model `{status:"ok",service:"dogwatch-api",version}`.
- `problems.py`: RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with `type urn:dogwatch:problem:<code>` (R-8). Codes not-found 404, method-not-allowed 405 (with `Allow`), validation-failed 422 (no input echoed), internal-error 500 (no traceback). Reserved code constants only.
- `middleware.py`: a pure ASGI RequestContextMiddleware. It echoes or generates `X-Request-ID` on every response, including 500s, using the pattern `^[\x20-\x7E]{1,128}$`. It times the request, emits exactly one C5 JSON log line per request (5xx lines include `error_type` and `error_traceback`; no bodies or query strings), and returns the catch-all 500 problem response when the response has not started.
- `log.py`: JSON stdout logger.
- `__main__.py`: binds the socket itself and passes it to `uvicorn.Server(...).run(sockets=[sock])` with `access_log=False`. On EADDRINUSE it prints `dogwatch-api: error: <host>:<port> is already in use; set DOGWATCH_API_PORT to choose another port` and exits 1.

Also add `scripts/bench_health.py`, an httpx async load generator that reports p95/p99/errors (SC-006). Tests follow V-A1…V-A4; the 422 case uses a test-only route registered on a `create_app()` instance inside tests. Deliverable: CP-2 for the API.
acceptance_criteria: `make lint-api` and `make test-api` pass in a clean clone with only uv installed, and need no environment variables or credentials.

V-A1: GET `/api/v1/health` returns 200 `application/json` `{"status":"ok","service":"dogwatch-api","version":"0.1.0"}` with no auth. GET `/api/v1/openapi.json` returns a document whose `openapi` field starts with `3.1`. `/docs` and `/redoc` return 404.

V-A2: an unknown path returns a 404 problem+json with code `not-found` and the path without the query string. POST to health returns 405 with an `Allow` header. A test-only validation route returns 422 `validation-failed` without echoing input. A route that raises returns 500 `internal-error` whose body has no traceback or exception text.

V-A3: a valid `X-Request-ID` is echoed. Oversized or control-character IDs are replaced with a UUID4. Every response, including 404/405/500, carries `X-Request-ID`. Exactly one JSON log line is written per request (including 500), with fields ts, level, event, request_id, method, route (template or null), status and duration_ms, and no query string.
V-A4: defaults resolve to 127.0.0.1:8000. `DOGWATCH_API_PORT=0` or `=abc` exits 1 with a message naming the variable. A port already in use produces the documented message and exit 1.
`make run-api` serves on 127.0.0.1:8000, and `curl` to `/api/v1/health` returns the health body.
`make bench-api` runs and prints p95, p99 and error count. Meeting SC-006 thresholds is checked at acceptance in EPIC-006.

epics.title: React web shell with API status
epics.description:
Owns WP-W. Exclusive write scope: `web/**`. Create the `dogwatch-web` pnpm project: - `package.json`: - `private`, `type: module`, `packageManager pnpm@11.x.y`, `engines.node 24.x` - the C9 `browserslist` field - scripts with these EXACT names (C7 seam): `dev`, `build`, `test`, `lint`, `format`, `preview` - `lint` = prettier --check, eslint, stylelint on src/**/*.css, tsc --noEmit - `build` = tsc --noEmit, vite build, node scripts/check-build.mjs - `test` = vitest run - `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.node-version` (24.x), and `.env.example` with `VITE_DOGWATCH_API_BASE_URL=/api/v1` - `vite.config.ts`: - React plugin; `build.manifest: true`; content-hashed assets - `build.target` and `build.cssTarget` from `browserslistToEsbuild()` (R-6) - dev server and preview on 127.0.0.1:5173 with strictPort, proxying `/api` to 127.0.0.1:8000 - vitest with jsdom and the setup file - Lint config: - strict tsconfig - ESLint flat config with typescript-eslint, react-hooks and jsx-a11y; `no-restricted-globals`/`no-restricted-properties` forbid `document.cookie`, `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` - Prettier - stylelint with `stylelint-declaration-strict-value`, which forces colour, spacing and font values to come from tokens; media params are exempt Source: - `index.html`: `lang="en"`, title Dogwatch, viewport meta, a single module script with `src`. - `router.ts`: maps pathname to `/` → HomeView and anything else → NotFoundView, with an `` Home link. No router library. - `strings.ts`: English copy. - `api/health.ts`: `fetchHealth` per C8, using a 5 s `AbortSignal.timeout` combined via `AbortSignal.any`. The result is `available` only for ok + JSON + `status==="ok"`. Response text is never rendered. - `components/ApiStatus.tsx`: one fetch per mount; the cleanup aborts. Renders `

`. The state is terminal, so a late resolve is ignored. - `components/ErrorBoundary.tsx`: shows "Something went wrong" and a reload button. - Views have one h1 each. - `styles/tokens.css` puts tokens on `:root`, light theme only, with contrast ratios ≥ 4.5:1 documented in comments. `global.css` sets focus-visible outlines, breakpoints at 640 and 1024, and 320 px reflow. Also: - `scripts/check-build.mjs` per C9: KB = 1000 bytes; gzip level 9 of the entry chunk plus its transitive static imports must be ≤ 100000 bytes; total CSS gzip ≤ 20000 bytes; no inline `
acceptance_criteria: `make install-web lint-web test-web build-web` passes in a clean clone with only Node 24 and pnpm 11 installed, and needs no credentials or running API.

V-W1 (`ApiStatus.test.tsx`) covers: initial "Checking API…"; "API available" for `{status:"ok"}`; "API unavailable" for non-2xx, non-JSON, `status≠ok`, network throw, and a 5 s timeout using fake timers; a late success after timeout is ignored; exactly one fetch call per mount; the live region has role=status.
V-W2 (`App.test.tsx`): `/` renders Home, and `/nope` renders "Page not found" with a link whose href is `/`.
V-W3 (`ErrorBoundary.test.tsx`): a throwing child renders "Something went wrong" and a reload button.
V-W4 (`a11y.test.tsx`): axe with tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa reports 0 violations on Home and Not Found. Each view has exactly one h1 and header/main landmarks.

V-W5: `check-build.mjs` exits 0 on the real build. It exits 1 on a synthetic over-budget fixture and on an injected inline `<script>`; both cases are exercised by a unit test or a documented manual check recorded in the PR.
V-W6: a hard-coded hex colour in a `.css` file fails `make lint-web` (stylelint). `localStorage.setItem` in a `.tsx` file fails ESLint.
`make run-web` serves on 127.0.0.1:5173, and with `make run-api` running the page shows "API available".

epics.title: Minimal fixture project and golden harness
epics.description:
Owns WP-F. Exclusive write scope: `fixtures/**` and `scanner/tests/golden/**`. Must not edit `scanner/src/**` or `scanner/pyproject.toml`; the `golden` marker and `scanner/tests/__init__.py` are provided by EPIC-002. Escalate scanner defects to EPIC-002 rather than patching them.

Create:
- `fixtures/README.md` documenting convention C12: `fixtures/<kebab-name>/` holds `dogwatch.toml`, the source tree and `expected-report.json`; fixtures are static data and are never installed, imported or executed.
- `fixtures/minimal/dogwatch.toml` per C2, with `name="acme_shop"` and `root="src"`.
- `fixtures/minimal/src/acme_shop/{__init__,orders,payments}.py`, which are inert stubs.
- `fixtures/minimal/expected-report.json`, generated only by `regenerate.py`.

Under `scanner/tests/golden/`:
- `__init__.py`.
- `harness.py`: discovers every `fixtures/*/dogwatch.toml` relative to the repo root and runs `[sys.executable, "-m", "dogwatch", "check", "--config", <abs>, "--output", <tmp>]` in a subprocess.
- `test_fixture_goldens.py`:
  - All tests carry `@pytest.mark.golden`.
  - Parametrized over 5 environment variants (TZ and LC_ALL/LANG pairs as in plan §8 WP-F notes), each with a distinct temporary cwd and HOME and a random PYTHONHASHSEED.
  - Asserts byte equality with `expected-report.json` and prints a `difflib.unified_diff` on mismatch.
  - Asserts the golden file's bytes and mtime are unchanged after the run (V-F2).
  - Asserts the `dogwatch` console script resolves.
- `regenerate.py`: run via `python -m tests.golden.regenerate`; the only code that writes golden files (FR-034).

This epic also owns the integration seam for the version string: the golden file embeds scanner 0.1.0. Fixture source data has no dependency and may be drafted early. Generating the golden file requires EPIC-002. Deliverable: CP-3.
acceptance_criteria: `make test-fixtures` runs only golden-marked tests and passes. `make test-scanner` does not collect or run them.
`UV_PYTHON=3.11 make test-fixtures` and `UV_PYTHON=3.14 make test-fixtures` both pass locally on macOS, giving 5 variants × 2 interpreters = 10 byte-identical runs (SC-002 local half).

`fixtures/minimal/expected-report.json` validates against `scanner/schemas/report-0.1.schema.json`. It has `findings: []`, `policy.path: "dogwatch.toml"`, and `policy.digest.sha256` equal to `shasum -a 256 fixtures/minimal/dogwatch.toml`.
Changing one byte of `expected-report.json` makes `make test-fixtures` fail with a unified diff in the output. Reverting the byte makes it pass again.
`make regen-fixtures` rewrites the golden file to identical bytes, so `git diff --exit-code fixtures/` is clean, and the golden test itself never writes to `fixtures/`.
`make run-scanner` prints a report to stdout that is byte-identical to `fixtures/minimal/expected-report.json`.

`git check-attr eol -- fixtures/minimal/expected-report.json` reports `lf`, and no `.py` file under `fixtures/` is opened or imported by the scanner (covered by EPIC-002 V-S7 and re-asserted here by running the CLI against the fixture).

epics.title: CI workflow, quickstart README, acceptance
epics.description:
Owns WP-I. Exclusive write scope: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `README.md`. This is the only epic allowed to amend `Makefile` after EPIC-001, and only to fix contract drift found during integration. Area code defects are escalated to the owning epic.

Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) per C10:
- Triggers: `pull_request` and `push` on `main`. No `pull_request_target`.
- Top-level `permissions: contents: read`. `concurrency` group `ci-<PR number or ref>` with `cancel-in-progress`.
- Actions pinned to full 40-character SHAs with `# vX.Y.Z` comments, resolved via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/ref/tags/<tag>`:
  - `actions/checkout`
  - `astral-sh/setup-uv` (`version-file: scanner/pyproject.toml`, `enable-cache`)
  - `pnpm/action-setup` (`package_json_file: web/package.json`)
  - `actions/setup-node` (`node-version-file: web/.node-version`, `cache: pnpm`, `cache-dependency-path: web/pnpm-lock.yaml`)
- Jobs, each with `timeout-minutes: 10`:
  - `scanner` on ubuntu-24.04, matrix python [3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14] via the `UV_PYTHON` env. `make lint-scanner` runs only on 3.11, then `make test-scanner`.
  - `api` on ubuntu-24.04: `make lint-api test-api`.
  - `web` on ubuntu-24.04: `make install-web lint-web test-web build-web`.
  - `fixtures` on os [ubuntu-24.04, macos-15] × python [3.11, 3.14]: `make test-fixtures`.
- R-1 rule: if CPython 3.15.0 final has been published when this work starts, and EPIC-002 has adopted it, add 3.15 to the scanner matrix and use it as the newest fixtures entry.

README.md: at most 80 lines, following the C11 section budget:
- intro
- prerequisites (make, uv 0.12.x, Node 24.x, pnpm 11.x, scanner CPython 3.11–3.14, macOS/Linux only)
- install/test/lint/format commands
- per-area run/test/lint/format table
- defaults (API 127.0.0.1:8000, web 5173, environment variables from C6)
- "Direction for later tickets (provisional)", one or two lines each covering FR-046, 057, 062, 082, 090, 092, 093
- branch protection and the recovery runbook

Then run the acceptance checkpoints CP-4 and CP-5 and record the results in the PR description.
acceptance_criteria: `ci.yml` passes `actionlint` or an equivalent YAML/schema check. `grep -n 'secrets\.' .github/workflows/ci.yml` and `grep -n pull_request_target` both return nothing. Every `uses:` line matches `@[0-9a-f]{40} # v`. Top-level `permissions` is exactly `contents: read` (V-I1).

Job and status names match C10: `scanner (3.11)`…`scanner (3.14)`, `api`, `web`, and `fixtures (<os>, <py>)` × 4. On the integration PR all statuses are green, and the summed runner-minutes are ≤ 25 with wall-clock ≤ 10 min (CP-4, FR-095).
Every CI step calls a root Makefile target, with no inline duplicates of lint or test commands (FR-089).

`wc -l README.md` is ≤ 80. The README documents one command each for test-all, lint-all and format-all, the per-area commands for scanner, api, web and fixtures, and labels every "Direction" item provisional (SC-010).
From a fresh clone on macOS, with only make, uv, Node 24 and pnpm 11 present: `make install && make lint && make test && make build-web` succeeds with no credentials in ≤ 10 minutes (V-I3, SC-001).

V-I2: throwaway branches, each seeding one ruff format violation, one prettier violation, one eslint or stylelint violation and one golden-byte change, each turn exactly the matching CI status red. The results are recorded in the PR.

Acceptance measurements are recorded in the PR: `make bench-api` gives p95 ≤ 50 ms, p99 ≤ 100 ms and 0 errors (V-A5); Lighthouse mobile median of 3 on `pnpm preview` gives LCP ≤ 2.5 s, CLS ≤ 0.1, TBT ≤ 200 ms and an accessibility contrast pass (V-W7); on 3.10, `pip install ./scanner` is refused (V-S8).

risk_notes: Parallelism: wave 1 is EPIC-001 alone. Wave 2 is EPIC-002, EPIC-003 and EPIC-004 together (3 slots). Wave 3 is EPIC-005, which may draft fixture source data early but needs EPIC-002 to generate the golden file. Wave 4 is EPIC-006. The critical path is EPIC-001 → EPIC-002 → EPIC-005 → EPIC-006.

Seam with high conflict risk: `scanner/pyproject.toml` and `scanner/tests/__init__.py` belong to EPIC-002 only. EPIC-005 depends on the pre-registered `golden` marker (with `--strict-markers`) and on `tests/__init__.py` existing, so `python -m tests.golden.regenerate` and pytest import `tests.golden` the same way. If either is missing, EPIC-005 must escalate to EPIC-002 instead of editing those files.

Seam: the C7 Makefile is written in full by EPIC-001 before any area exists. EPIC-004 must use the exact `package.json` script names dev/build/test/lint/format/preview. EPIC-002 and EPIC-003 must keep ruff, mypy and pytest runnable with no arguments. Any drift is fixed only by EPIC-006.
Version coupling: the golden file embeds scanner version 0.1.0 and the policy digest. Any version bump or edit to `fixtures/minimal/dogwatch.toml` needs `make regen-fixtures` in the same PR.

R-1, CPython 3.15: final release is scheduled for 2026-10-09, after the plan date. Use 3.11–3.14 unless 3.15 is final when EPIC-002 starts and mypy, ruff and pytest install cleanly on it. Otherwise keep the 3.14 ceiling and note it in the PR.

Toolchain freshness: pnpm 11 defaults `minimumReleaseAge` to 1 day, and Vite 8, Rolldown and the stylelint plugins may resolve differently on different days. The committed lockfiles are authoritative, and CI uses `--frozen-lockfile` / `--locked`.

TOML error messages differ across 3.11–3.14 (R-5), and `ru_maxrss` units differ between macOS and Linux (V-S6). Tests must assert only on prefix, path and line, and must normalise units, or the matrix will flake.

The golden test's locale variants (tr_TR.UTF-8, en_US.UTF-8) may be missing on ubuntu-24.04 runners. The scanner never reads the locale, so setting an unavailable locale is harmless, but the harness must not fail when the locale is not installed.
axe in jsdom cannot evaluate colour contrast (R-7). Contrast is covered only by token choice and the Lighthouse acceptance run, not by CI.
Action SHAs can only be resolved with network and `gh` access during EPIC-006. If that is unavailable, the implementer must stop and escalate rather than use tags.
verification_strategy:
Verification is layered and runs through the Makefile, so local and CI behaviour match.

1. Per-epic gates: CP-1 for EPIC-001, CP-2 for EPIC-002/003/004 (`make lint-<area> test-<area>` in a clean clone with only that area's toolchain), and CP-3 for EPIC-005 (`make test-fixtures` under UV_PYTHON 3.11 and 3.14).
2. Integration: EPIC-006 runs CP-4, where the PR shows all 10 C10 statuses green within the ≤10 min / ≤25 runner-minute budget. It then runs CP-5 acceptance and records the results in the PR: timed clean clone (SC-001), the 10-run determinism matrix on Linux and macOS (SC-002), seeded-failure PRs (SC-004), bench-api p95/p99 (SC-006), the check-build budget (SC-007), Lighthouse (SC-008), axe at 0 violations (SC-009), README ≤ 80 lines (SC-010), no secrets in the workflow (SC-011), and the 3.10 install refusal (SC-012).
3. Coverage: the verification matrix maps each requirement to a test file and CI job (V-S1…V-S8, V-F1/F2, V-A1…A5, V-W1…W7, V-I1…I4). The developer stage should create one task per V-ID. SC-005 (DORA lead time, V-I4) can only be measured after merge, over 30 days, and is out of scope for this run.
missing_info_requests: Non-blocking (default applied: `dogwatch: error: <message>` with no ID): should output-write and output-equals-config failures get catalogued diagnostic IDs such as `dogwatch:output-unwritable` in the CD-3 catalogue? (R-2)

Non-blocking (default applied): confirm that the scanner's upper CPython bound depends on whether 3.15.0 final (scheduled 2026-10-09) is out when EPIC-002 starts, and that falling back to 3.14 is acceptable if dev tools lack 3.15 wheels. (R-1)
Non-blocking (default applied): confirm that 'dotted name split across roots' means the same `name` declared under different `root` values. (R-3)
Which GitHub repository (owner/name) will host CI? It is needed to run the fork-PR check (V-I1) and to recommend branch protection. Pinning action SHAs only needs the upstream action repos.
